rollback.evidence: Applied twice on the managed-Supabase shape (pgcrypto in the extensions schema, public.digest proven absent before anything is applied) on PostgreSQL 16.14 and 17.10 with identical migration and verification bytes, via scripts/verify-m63-legal-signability.sh. Each run first proves the PRE-M63 constraint refuses all four new categories, so the blocker is measured rather than assumed, then seeds historical legal rows (three document versions and one real signature bound to a published version and its exact content hash), then applies M63 twice at psql exit 0. The seeded rows are byte-identical after both passes, compared by a full-row fingerprint taken before the first apply, and the row counts are unchanged. The verification suite proves by REAL INSERTS on BOTH tables that all 20 categories are accepted and a 21st is refused, that a draft of a newly added category still cannot be signed, that the append-only and published-only signature triggers and the one-published-version-per-category index are intact, and that no probe row survives. A bare database proves the preflight fails closed. NOT AN UNCONDITIONAL ROLLBACK: narrowing the constraint is only safe while no version or signature uses one of the four new categories, and the application half (the four DocumentCategory values and the four manifest mappings) must roll back with it, because they are one change.

migrations.notes: Widens the single-column category CHECK on public.research_fm_document_versions and public.research_fm_document_signatures from 16 to 20 values so the four REQUIRED counsel-approved documents that mapped to no category (XR-LEGAL-12, XR-LEGAL-13, XR-LEGAL-14, XR-LEGAL-15) can hold a published version and bind a signature. The original sixteen values are preserved in order; nothing is renamed, removed or transformed. Constraints are dropped by structural discovery and recreated under one canonical name, so a second apply is a no-op in effect. Writes no row and publishes nothing: no document version, signature, legal package, binding, attestation, customer, settlement or supplier fact. appliedToProduction stays false and managedMigrationId stays PENDING until an authenticated production read confirms otherwise.

rollback.evidence: Applied twice on the managed-Supabase shape (pgcrypto in the extensions schema, public.digest proven absent before anything is applied) on PostgreSQL 16.14 and 17.10 with identical migration and verification bytes, via scripts/verify-m64-shipping-commitments.sh. Each run first proves the routine does NOT exist before M64 and that service_role has no direct SELECT on research_early_access_cart_settlement_hardening or research_early_access_cart_fulfilment_events, so the blocker M64 exists to close is measured rather than assumed. A database without the M62 cart schema proves the preflight fails closed with SQLSTATE 55000 and leaves no routine behind. M64 then applies twice at psql exit 0, with the 25-assertion behavioural suite green after each apply, the public relation count unchanged across both applies and every research_* table still empty afterwards. The suite proves the routine is STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path-pinned, that PUBLIC, anon and authenticated cannot execute it while service_role can, that no role gained direct SELECT on any M62 table, and by real fixtures that a due active checkout is reported as processing, a future commitment is excluded, a superseded checkout is excluded, a fully shipped due commitment is reported with stage shipped rather than hidden, a part-shipped one as partially_shipped, a voided shipment stops counting as shipped, the ordering is deterministic and byte-identical across calls, and that no customer, supplier, payment, proof or transaction fact leaves the routine. ROLLBACK IS ORDERED, NOT UNCONDITIONAL: dropping the routine makes SupabaseEarlyAccessShippingSlaStore.dueBy throw, so the application half (the durable store, the alert sink and the worker composition) must be withdrawn first or the 72-hour monitor fails on every tick. Dropping it destroys no data, because the routine owns none.

migrations.notes: Additive, read-only. Creates ONE security-definer routine, public.research_early_access_cart_shipping_commitments_due(timestamptz), so the 72-hour shipping SLA monitor has a durable, list-shaped work list. It exists because M62 revokes every one of its tables from service_role and grants no routine that enumerates cart checkouts, leaving the monitor undrivable by any production composition. THE M62 BOUNDARY IS NOT WIDENED: no table gains a SELECT grant, EXECUTE is granted to service_role alone, and the migration's own post-condition refuses to commit if service_role has direct SELECT on either table it reads. Creates no table, column, index, trigger or type; writes no row of any kind; changes no existing routine and does not touch M61, M62 or M63. It reports the durable shipment stage and decides no overdue-ness, so the rule that a shipped order is never overdue stays in earlyAccessIsOverdue and is not restated in SQL. appliedToProduction stays false and managedMigrationId stays PENDING until an authenticated production read confirms otherwise.

rollback.evidence: Applied twice on the managed-Supabase shape (pgcrypto in the extensions schema, public.digest proven absent before anything is applied) on PostgreSQL 16 and 17 with identical migration and verification bytes, via scripts/verify-m65-quantity-band.sh. Each run first proves BOTH tables really do carry exactly one 'quantity <= 3' band before M65, so the blocker is measured rather than assumed, and seeds a REAL cart item at the old ceiling (quantity 3, subtotal 3000, discount 600, payable 2400) with the harness aborting if that seed did not land, so the 'existing rows preserved' assertions cannot pass vacuously over an empty table. A database without the cart schema proves the preflight fails closed with SQLSTATE 55000 and leaves no constraint behind. M65 then applies twice at psql exit 0, with the 14-assertion behavioural suite green after each apply, the seeded row byte-identical afterwards, the public relation count unchanged, and every check constraint OUTSIDE the two named tables byte-identical before and after. The suite proves the canonical band exists and is named on both tables, that no 1..3 band survives on either, that the subtotal = unit_price_cents * quantity identity and the unrelated line_index and unit_price_cents constraints all survive, that the reservation quantity domain is NOT widened, and by real durable inserts that a cart item of quantity 20 is accepted while 21 is refused by the database, and a child release is accepted at 20 and refused at both 0 and 21. The behavioural fixtures run inside a transaction that is rolled back, because research_early_access_cart_child_releases carries an append-only trigger and its evidence rows cannot be deleted. The lower bound is exercised on the child-release table rather than the item table on purpose: a cart item of quantity 0 can never insert whatever the band says, since the subtotal identity forces subtotal_cents to 0 and both discount_cents < subtotal_cents and payable_cents > 0 are then unsatisfiable, so a refusal there would prove nothing about the band. ROLLBACK IS ORDERED, NOT UNCONDITIONAL: narrowing back to 1..3 fails validation once any durable row sits above three, so the application half must be withdrawn first and both tables proven clear; if they are not, the band stays at 1..20 while the application refuses above three, which is the safe divergence. Rolling back destroys no data: the migration widens a constraint and copies no rows.

migrations.notes: Additive and non-destructive. Widens exactly two CHECK constraints, both on a quantity column, from 1..3 to 1..20: public.research_early_access_cart_items.quantity and public.research_early_access_cart_child_releases.quantity. The lower bound is unchanged, so zero and negative stay refused. It exists because the round now accepts up to twenty units of one exact variant, and until these two bands are widened a checkout for four units is accepted by every layer of the application and then rejected by the database at the last moment, after the customer has already been quoted. It creates no table, column, index, trigger, type or routine, writes no row of any kind, grants and revokes nothing, and changes no existing routine. It touches neither M61, M62, M63 nor M64. The existing constraints are auto-named, so the migration finds each one by its normalized BAND SHAPE (requiring both bound comparisons) rather than by name, which is why the subtotal_cents = unit_price_cents * quantity identity that mentions the same column is left untouched; it then replaces each with an explicitly NAMED constraint so future migrations can address it directly. It refuses to run if either table is absent, if a table carries no quantity band or more than one, or if any existing row already sits outside the new band. Re-runnable: a second apply finds the band already canonical and does nothing. It widens no unrelated quantity: the inventory, reservation, supplier-operations and persistent-cart tables carry their own quantity constraints and are deliberately not named. appliedToProduction stays false and managedMigrationId stays PENDING until an authenticated production read confirms otherwise.

Every dependency must exist and be applied before its dependent migration.

Checksums are computed from canonical Git blob bytes at the reviewed source SHA/path, not platform-normalized worktree line endings; a distinct managed path must byte-match that source.
Every migration requires a non-empty rollback strategy, procedure, and verification evidence.

Pending migrations in this DAG create no operational product, price, inventory, lot, COA, order, role, or Care records. The strength gate's only reviewed seed is the non-operational founder-locked dispute registry public.research_catalog_founder_locked_variant.

Every checked-in managed migration file is represented exactly once. Pending nodes pin immutable Git bytes, remain appliedToProduction false with managedMigrationId PENDING, and do not imply production application.

The protected order requires both reservation commands and the variant strength write gate before persistent cart, followed by fulfillment supplier operations -> affiliate professional operations -> pricing lineage -> RLS retro hardening.
No pending migration may be marked applied until the authenticated managed ledger shows its exact version and the post-apply security, privilege, row-count, and dependency invariants pass.
